fieldNotes.site: Ball's existing aluminum beverage-can plant at ~395 West Hermitage Rd NE, Rome (Floyd County), off GA-53 in the Northwest Regional Industrial Park. Complex = a grey-roof warehouse/finished-goods hall (rotated NW-SE) connected to a white-roof process/manufacturing hall on the SW (heavy rooftop equipment). Ball's newer aluminum CUPS plant sits adjacent to the SW (separate Ball facility) -> multipleFacilities true.
fieldNotes.canVsCups: Roster idx 15 = the CANS plant (the older, existing beverage-can plant). The adjacent aluminum-cups plant (2020, ~180 jobs) is a distinct building and NOT this audited site.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Single entrance drive off West Hermitage Rd opening onto a large internal apron; no guard booth or barrier arm visible at the throat -> classed no-gate/no-guard, flagged medium (a gatehouse could exist but is not visible in imagery).
fieldNotes.docks: Docks split across two faces: the grey warehouse's SE (rail-side) apron (finished-can outbound) and the white process hall's SW face (coil/inbound). ~18 doors total; shipRcvSeparate true (flagged).
fieldNotes.railServed: A freight mainline runs immediately along the east property edge but no spur enters the site -> false (spur-add feasible).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: NW Rome/Floyd County industrial park, fields/woods and Berry College nearby -> Rural (small-city edge). Cell coverage fine (GA-53 corridor).
fieldNotes.buildingCount: 2 connected masses (warehouse + process hall) counted for this can-plant site; the adjacent cups plant is excluded from this site's count.

citations.claim: Ball's own Feb-2025 locations map lists Rome, GA as an operating site.
Ball's new aluminum-cups plant to be built adjacent to Ball's EXISTING aluminum beverage-can manufacturing plant in Rome/Floyd County.

verification.rationale: Ball's existing Rome can plant is current per Ball's own 2025 locations map and is explicitly referenced as the 'existing' plant in the 2019 cups-plant announcement; not among Ball's closures.
